subject: Integration: Third-Party Compliance Data Transfer & Triage Model

From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@aishaconsult.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration: Third-Party Compliance Data Transfer & Triage Model

Hi Vanessa / Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Aisha Consulting will be the technical integrator for several of our mutual customers and we're seeing two recurring asks: (1) a lightweight, auditable path for SOC2/evidence handoffs from partners into vendor GRC systems, and (2) a triage/incident model for when a partner delivers a pen-test or infra finding that requires coordinated remediation.

We put together a short proposal for a "handoff + triage" workflow that minimizes manual uploads and preserves provenance (timestamps, signer, scope). High level: S3 drop + signed manifest OR direct connector to partner GRC with signed webhook receipts, automated validation of manifest schema, and a small triage SLA matrix (severity -> owner -> escalation timeline).

Can your security or partner team take a look? We're happy to pilot this with a single customer. Suggested attendees for the kickoff: Redwood security lead, Redwood SOC2 owner, Aisha SecOps lead, and one delivery PM.

Attached: evidence_transfer_template.xlsx (stub), triage_runbook_draft.md (stub).

Best,
Sara Khan
Head of Integrations
Aisha Consulting
Attachments: evidence_transfer_template.xlsx (spreadsheet), triage_runbook_draft.md (text)

Forwarding Sara's note and my quick internal take. Quoted below.

We need to cover three commercial/operational points before the kickoff:
1) Contract scope: is the connector covered under the standard partner SOW or will it be a billable integration? I suspect Aisha will want an SOW + success criteria.
2) Liability & evidence retention: SOC2 evidence retention windows differ by customer — we need the addendum to allow per-customer retention policies and clear ownership of backups.
3) Incident escalation: recommend we propose a 72/24/8 SLA ladder (informal -> assigned -> emergency), documented in the triage_runbook.

Neha — can security own the checklist items (SFTP fingerprinting, webhook signing) and confirm whether redaction/pseudonymization guidance is required? Marcus — can you draft an ops handoff sequence (3 bullets) we can send to Aisha pre-call?

Thanks — Priyom

Sara — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and action items (see below). We can use this thread as the canonical record for attachments and the demo timeline.

Meeting minutes (high level):
- Agreed pilot approach: Aisha will push sample manifests into S3; Redwood will validate manifests and return signed receipts. If manifest validation fails, Redwood will provide structured error output for automated remediation.
- Triage ladder: Inform (72h), Investigate (24h), Escalate (8h) — severity mapping in triage_runbook_draft.md
- Data handling: partners send evidence encrypted; Redwood will store customer evidence per customer retention policy and will redact PII on ingest if requested in the addendum.

Action items / owners: 
- Aisha (Sara): provide sample manifests + one pen-test sample by Mon 2026-09-28.
- Redwood (Marcus): ops handoff sequence and connector runbook (due 2026-10-02).
- Redwood (Neha): security checklist and webhook signing spec (due 2026-09-30).
- Redwood (Priyom): draft partner addendum + redline summary (circulating by 2026-09-29).

Attachments included in this thread: evidence_transfer_template.xlsx, triage_runbook_draft.md, redline-summary.docx (stubs). Also linking the pilot intake doc: https://drive.redwood.com/partners/aisha/evidence-flow and the JIRA ticket SECINTEG-412 for tracking.
